questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
A student keeps a compass needle at a fixed point near a long straight copper wire.
Assertion 1: Increasing the current through the wire increases the magnitude of the magnetic field at the point where the needle is kept.
Reason 1: The deflection of the compass needle kept at that point increases when the current through the wire is increased. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
A student bends a straight copper wire into a circular loop, connects it to a battery and places a compass needle at the centre of the loop.
Assertion 1: The needle shows a deflection, because every section of the loop contributes to the magnetic field lines in the same direction within the loop.
Reason 1: The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is zero, because the field of each section of the loop acts there in a direction opposite to that of the others. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

questions.subject: Science
questions.stem:
A student holds a current-carrying straight conductor in one hand so that the thumb points towards the direction of the current, and notes the way in which the fingers of that hand wrap around the conductor.
Assertion 1: The way in which those fingers wrap around the conductor gives the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field around it.
Reason 1: The magnetic field around a current-carrying straight wire is made up of straight lines running parallel to the wire. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.
